title: David Pours Out the Water from Bethlehem
text:
During the wars with the Philistines, David was at his stronghold near the cave of Adullam, while a Philistine garrison held his home town of Bethlehem and their army was camped in the valley of Rephaim. It was harvest time.

David, homesick and thirsty, spoke a wish aloud: "Oh, that someone would give me a drink of water from the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate!" It was not an order, only a longing.

Three of his mighty warriors heard him. They broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well by Bethlehem's gate, and carried it back to David.

David would not drink it. Instead he poured it out on the ground as an offering to the Lord. "Far be it from me, O Lord, that I should do this," he said. "Is this not the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?" And he refused to drink it.
lesson: People will sometimes take real risks just to please you. Treat their effort as precious, and never enjoy a privilege that others have paid for with danger as if it were your due.
